sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Transport activity assay: insertion at 423 produced a functional mutant (activity preserved). Surface immunofluorescence confirmed extracellular location of the HA tag.
sites.rationale: Residue 423 lies within ECL1 (computed extracellular span 416-427), 8 residues from TM1 end (415) and 5 residues from TM2 start (428), satisfying the >=3 residue buffer on both sides. The paper directly reports HA insertion at residue 423 is extracellular (non-permeabilized cell staining) and functionally tolerated (transport activity preserved). Python-verified: seq[422]='I', seq[423]='Q', consistent with insert_after_residue=423. Full-length ABCG2 with HA tag inserted after residue 423 expressed in mammalian cells; surface accessibility tested by immunofluorescence in non-permeabilized cells (PMC2649121).

sources.claim: Insertions at residues 423, 454, 462, 499, 529, 532, and 651 produced functional mutants, whereas insertions at residues 560, 594, and 623 resulted in mutants with significantly reduced activity and insertions at residues 387, 420, 474, and 502 completely abrogated the activity. HA tags inserted at residues 387, 474, 529, 532, 560, and 651 were localized intracellularly, whereas those inserted at residues 420, 423, 454, 499, 502, 594, and 623 revealed an extracellular location. Residue 462 was localized in a transmembrane (TM) segment.

sites.evidence_type: topology inference (C-terminal snorkel — no accessible terminus)
sites.rationale: C-terminus not extracellular (topology 'I' at residue L) and no accessible N-terminus — C-terminal snorkel presents the tag on the surface via a TM-snorkeling linker (fallback: no natively accessible terminus)

literature_notes: L1 (PMC2649121) is the primary evidence source, reporting HA tag insertions at 13 positions in full-length ABCG2. Two positions (423 in ECL1, 499 in ECL2) are both extracellular (non-permeabilized immunofluorescence) and functionally tolerated (transport activity preserved). Position 454 is reported as extracellular and functional by the paper but falls within the computed intracellular span (449-477); per the authoritative topology landmarks, it is classified as intracellular and placed in other_positions. Positions 420, 502, 594, and 623 are extracellular per the paper but abrogate or significantly reduce transport activity; they are placed in other_positions. L2-L5 (PMC9917445) report N-terminal GFP-tagged ABCG2 with preserved expression, surface display, and transport function. However, ABCG2's N-terminus (residue 1) is intracellular per the computed topology (INTRACELLULAR: 1-394); an N-terminal GFP fusion is therefore an intracellular tag, not an extracellular surface tag, and does not qualify as a surface site. L6-L9 (PMC10941402, PMC10327217) report N-terminal FLAG tags on zebrafish ABCG2 homologs; same reasoning applies — N-terminus is intracellular. L10 (PMC7900420) reports N-terminal SBP tag in a RUSH trafficking study; again intracellular. Position 560 is in the computed extracellular ECL3 (557-627) but the paper reports it as intracellular with reduced activity; it is placed in other_positions as abrogates_function.
